extracted text: The document describes three aluminum alloys: Al 7075-T6, Al 2024-T3, and Al 1050-H24, which were used to create two multilayer laminates (ALH19 and ADH19) by hot roll bonding. The T6 temper for Al 7075 involved solution treating at 465°C for 30 minutes, followed by water quenching and age hardening at 135°C for 14 hours. For Al 2024, the T6 temper involved solution treating at 490°C for 30 minutes, water quenching and age hardening at 160°C for 6 hours. The H24 temper involves work hardening followed by partial annealing (240°C).
property mapping:
UTS* (MPa) = Ultimate tensile strength in MPa
YS* (MPa) = Yield strength in MPa
HV = Vickers hardness
Elongation* (Pct) = Elongation percentage
T6 = Solution treating followed by quenching and peak age hardening
T3 = Solution treating followed by quenching, cold working, and natural aging
H24 = Work hardening followed by partial annealing (240°C)
abbreviations:
D = Al 7075 alloy
L = Al 2024 alloy
H = Al 1050 alloy
ALH19 = Laminate made of alternated Al 2024 and Al 1050 layers
ADH19 = Laminate made of alternated Al 7075 and Al 1050 layers
UTS = Ultimate tensile strength
YS = Yield stress
HV = Vickers hardness
Pct = Percentage
